# Thurbox

> Thurbox is a multi-session TUI for coding agents — Claude Code and Codex,
> through Fleet's harness profiles — running inside persistent tmux panes. Every
> session is a Fleet Task: Fleet starts it in the repository you pick and keeps
> it running, so sessions survive crashes and restarts. It is written in Rust,
> open source under the MIT license, and runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
> It can follow several Fleets, on this machine or on another one over ssh or
> WSL, as one list of sessions. Fleet's `fleet` command line drives the same
> sessions for scripting; `thurbox-cli` covers the interface's own files.
>
> Installing: run
> `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Thurbeen/thurbox/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`
> on Linux/macOS, or
> `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Thurbeen/thurbox/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex`
> on Windows. Both scripts also install `fleet`, `runtime-mux`, `runtime-herdr` and `workspace-git`.
> Nix (`nix profile install github:Thurbeen/thurbox`) ships `thurbox` and
> `thurbox-cli` only. Then run `fleet init` and `fleet service install --now`,
> then `thurbox`; with no Fleet config, its status line says to run `fleet init`. Config, themes and the interface itself are seeded on
> first launch.
>
> Its defining feature is that the interface is fully customizable: no UI is
> compiled into the binary. thurbox boots a Rust kernel that reads a
> directory of Lua files and draws whatever it finds, so every pane — the
> session list included — is a file the user can move, turn off, delete,
> rewrite, or install from someone else, with no recompile and no restart. The
> arrangement (`ui/layout.lua`), the Fleets it follows (`settings.toml`),
> themes, keybindings and settings are all data files. Because the interface is
> plain text in a directory, the usual way to change it is to ask a coding
> session for the change in English — the directory ships an `AGENTS.md` that
> tells whichever CLI is running how the interface is put together, so "add my
> project logs within a dedicated pane on the right in the thurbox UI" works
> from a session opened there. The same holds for orchestration:
> a session's agent can run `fleet`, so "using fleet, start refactor sessions
> for this repo, one per crate" spins up a fleet without a script.

## Docs

- [Documentation hub](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/index.html): entry point to all Thurbox documentation.
- [Tutorial](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/tutorial.html): onboarding walkthrough with screenshots — adding a repository to the picker, creating a first session in a repository, the everyday keybindings, and the equivalent fleet commands.
- [FAQ](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/faq.html): short answers to the most common questions (what it is, how it differs, install, platforms, license).
- [What is Fleet](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/fleet.html): Fleet, the engine — sessions as Tasks, resources and controllers, places and runtimes. Fleet runs on its own, headless, with no thurbox.
- [Install Fleet](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/fleet-install.html): Fleet alone — the install script, then `fleet init` and `fleet up`, and a systemd user unit that keeps `fleet up` running.
- [Get started with Fleet](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/fleet-get-started.html): install Fleet alone, a first Task, following it and reading its result.
- [Get started with Thurbox](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/thurbox-get-started.html): install, first launch, a first session and the essential keys.
- [Fleet reference](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/fleet/index.html): Fleet's architecture, contracts and configuration, one page per resource (Task, Session, TaskConfig, EnvProvider, ChangeRequest, Conversation, Listener, plugin kinds) and per controller (Task, ChangeRequest, Forge, Plugin, Gateway); the runtimes are at https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/runtime/index.html.
- [Fleet in herdr](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/runtime/herdr-users.html): for herdr users — a quick setup and a prompt for an agent, install Fleet (its installer ships runtime-herdr), add it to Fleet's config beside or instead of runtime-mux, run Tasks as herdr-core terminals that herdr's desktop app shows, find them with hc, run VEGA and its workers in herdr, and its limits.
- [Fleet features](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/fleet-features.html): sessions as Tasks, harness profiles, worktrees made by the runtime, places, messages between agents, the headless CLI.
- [What is thurbox](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/thurbox.html): thurbox, the terminal interface on top of one or more Fleets.
- [thurbox features](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/thurbox-features.html): the customizable interface, the session list, several Fleets, global search, layout, themes, notifications, settings.
- [Agents](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/agents.html): the agents are the harness profiles Fleet bundles (claude, codex, pi, opencode, kilo, omp, qwen, copilot, kimi).
- [Comparison](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/comparison.html): how Thurbox compares to Conductor, Claude Squad, Cursor, and other parallel coding-agent tools.
- [Installation](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/installation.html): install via curl, Homebrew, AUR, Nix/NixOS, winget, Chocolatey, or from source; prerequisites; running it; how to pin a specific version.
- [Orchestration](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/orchestration.html): Fleet, the engine in this repository that runs one session per Task — installing it, its Task loop, the Fleet Lens pane (https://github.com/Thurbeen/thurbox-fleetlens) that browses it from Thurbox, asking an agent to spin up sessions with fleet, and reading a session's state.
- [Configuration](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/configuration.html): every config file and knob — settings.toml and its [fleets] table, themes, keybindings, and environment variables.
- [The Interface](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/interface.html): every pane is an editable Lua mod — how to move, disable, replace or write one, how a mod reacts to events and puts actions in the Ctrl+P command palette, how to have a coding agent do it for you, what the kernel refuses a mod, and the panes you install (thurbox-code-review, thurbox-info-panel).
- [Architecture](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/architecture.html): the three components (thurbox, Fleet, the runtimes), Fleets and places, the Lua-on-Rust mod kernel and its five rules, module isolation, and the decisions behind them.
- [Recipes](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/recipes.html): a script that starts a session per package of a monorepo with fleet.

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Thurbeen/thurbox): source, README, and releases.
- [Keybindings](https://thurbox.thurbeen.eu/docs/keybindings.html): the Vim-inspired keyboard reference.
